title: Why does Python pass an instance to a class attribute that is a function?
q_body: I define a class attribute and give it a function. When I call this function, the instance is passed on as the first argument (as if it's an instance function call with a self ). I would not expect an instance to care that the attribute fn is a function, let alone for it to pass itself as an argument. Why does it do that? class BStatic: fn = None @staticmethod def static_fn(*args, **kwargs): print(args, kwargs) BStatic.fn = BStatic.static_fn bs = BStatic() bs.fn() # (<__main__.BStatic object at 0x0000022D63214590>,) {} BStatic.fn() # () {} In another example, I assigned a class attribute to a function defined on a module. When I call this function on an instance of a class, the instance is again passed as the first argument. class B: fn = None def instance_fn(self, *args, **kwargs): print(self, args, kwargs) def fn(*args, **kwargs): print(args, kwargs) B.fn = fn B.fn() # () {} b = B() b.fn() # (<__main__.B object at 0x0000022D643D23F0>,) {} This is not the case if I assign the class attribute on an instance. b.fn = fn b.fn() # () {}

title: Neural Network model in PyTorch prediction problem for anomaly detection in a simulated irrigation system
q_body: I'm working on my final studies project, which is detecting anomalies in an irrigation system. We simulated the irrigation network on a limited environment as you can see in the photo below. the model we created There is a PCB where an ESP32 microcontroller reads the values from the pressure sensor. In our model, 4 valves give us 2^4 = 16 combinations. My idea is to make it simple and create a simple neural network model using Pytorch that gets the state of valves as input (0 is off and 1 is on ex:0110) and one output, which is the pressure value. So that means our system will be predicting pressure from the valve combinations. The data set is created by getting certain valve combinations(using fractional factorial design), but I added other combinations like 1000, 0100, 0010, 00001, 1110, and 0111, and then it is augmented to get a large data set. here is the model : import torch import torch.nn as nn class PressureNeuralNet(nn.Module): def __init__(self, n_valves, hidden_size=32, dropout_rate=0.1): super().__init__() self.network = nn.Sequential( nn.Linear(n_valves, hidden_size), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout_rate), nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden_size, 1) ) def forward(self, x): return self.network(x) learning process: nn_model = PressureNeuralNet(n_valves) # Define loss and optimizers criterion = nn.MSELoss() nn_optimizer = optim.Adam(nn_model.parameters(), lr=0.01, weight_decay=1e-5) nn_scheduler = optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(nn_optimizer, mode='min', patience=5, factor=0.5, verbose=True) print("\nTraining Neural Network...") n

title: Track columns in pandas dataframe transformations
q_body: Say I have some dataset df where I know all the variables used beforehand. Also say I have some transformation called T1 that does something like df.loc[(df["col1"]> 4) & ((df["col3"]== 2)),"col2"] = 3 . Then T1 would use col1,col3 and whatever columns df.index is as input variables, and would have col2 as an output variable I would love to define a bunch of transformations T1 ... Ti and keep track of what columns they use as input and output variables without manually having to register the variables for every transformation. Bonus points if there is a way to resolve the variables before actually executing the command. My initial thought was to make a object read.col1 and write.col2 that when called yielded the column as text, but this also made read_cols=["col1","col2", *df.index] and write.cols=["col2"] and then could be blanked out with read.clear() etc after each transformation using a decorator around the function T1 that does the transformation. Then I would make a proxy object for df that exactly copied a pandas dataframe, but had a special flag that would make all commands pass if the flag was set so I could run through all functions, track variables, turn flag off then call the dataframe transformations for real on a second pass. But this seems quite convoluted and probably is not a good design pattern.
